title: Get Rich or Get Lucky: How a Startup Spin on the Art of Serendipity Can Change Your Career and Life
author: Max Schild
target_audience: Young professionals seeking unconventional career advice
Readers curious about the role of luck and serendipity in success
core_themes: The role of luck versus strategic action in wealth and success
Harnessing serendipity for career and business breakthroughs
Building networks and relationships that foster opportunity
Mindsets that attract luck and opportunity
primary_purpose: To explore how entrepreneurs and ambitious individuals can increase their chances for extraordinary success by simultaneously working hard, making smart bets, and cultivating the conditions for luck and serendipity to strike.

structure_format.narrative_style: Candid, conversational, streetwise with a blend of personal anecdotes and research-backed insights
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters combining case studies, startup stories, practical frameworks, and actionable advice
features: Action steps for fostering luck and recognizing opportunity
Breakdowns of famous tech founders’ journeys

key_concepts_lessons: Luck can be engineered by exposing oneself to more and varied opportunities.
Creating value and being visible increases your 'luck surface area.'
Serendipity favors those who take bold, persistent action.
Growth comes from embracing unlikely connections and spontaneous pivots.
Networking authentically and sharing your journey attracts the right people and ideas.
Failures and rejections often precede lucky breakthroughs—resilience matters.
notable_features: Blend of Silicon Valley mindset and actionable tips
Emphasis on both personal agency and chance
Up-to-date startup case studies and real-world applications
Exercises for readers to create their own luck
cultural_historical_context: Emerging from the tech startup boom of the 2010s and 2020s, the book addresses increasing interest in startups, tech success stories, and the debate over the relative importance of luck versus skill in achieving extraordinary results.
reception_impact: Quickly gaining traction among young entrepreneurs and founders
Praised for making the concept of luck actionable and demystifying startup successes
Critics note some overlap with established entrepreneurship advice, but appreciate the book’s fresh framing and practical outlook
comparable_titles: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant by Eric Jorgenson
Zero to One by Peter Thiel
The Lean Startup by Eric Ries
The Luck Factor by Richard Wiseman
